case.question: voluntary muscle definition
case.expected_answer: A muscle that can be controlled at will.
case.support_quote: Muscles that can be controlled at will are referred to as voluntary muscles.
case.source_qualification: Answer as stated in the supplied reference; no external fact verification.
family_reference_texts: A muscle may act ordinarily either under the control of the will or without conscious control. Muscles that can be controlled at will are referred to as voluntary muscles. Those that are not under the control of the will (volition) are called involuntary muscles. Examples of involuntary muscles are the smooth muscles, which are muscles lacking striations when viewed under a microscope. This is why involuntary muscles are sometimes called non-striated or un-striped muscles.

passages.text: voluntary muscle. noun, Anatomy. 1. muscle whose action is normally controlled by an individual's will; mainly skeletal muscle, composed of parallel bundles of striated, multinucleate fibers. This compound has an action on voluntary muscle causing gradual paralysis.

Definition. noun, plural: voluntary muscles. A muscle that can be controlled voluntarily. Supplement. Some of the muscles of the body may be controlled voluntarily.Other muscles act below the level of consciousness. Those muscles that can be controlled at one's will (volition) are called voluntary muscles.oun, plural: voluntary muscles. A muscle that can be controlled voluntarily. Supplement. Some of the muscles of the body may be controlled voluntarily.

According to the Encyclopedia Dictionary of Biology, voluntary muscles, also known as striated, skeletal or striped muscles, refer to muscles that are within a person’s control and are generally attached to the skeleton. An individual muscle is composed of bundles of long muscle fibers.

A voluntary muscle, often called a skeletal muscle, is one of three types of muscle in the body. Most voluntary muscles are used to move bones, though some, such as the muscles in the face, are used to create movements below the skin.

A voluntary muscle, often called a skeletal muscle, is one of three types of muscle in the body. Most voluntary muscles are used to move bones, though some, such as the muscles in the face, are used to create movements below the skin.he tongue is a voluntary muscle. A voluntary muscle also is called a skeletal muscle. A slight movement by one or more of the 43 facial muscles results in one of the many different expressions that humans can make.
